So following that line of logic, The Operative can be put under it, right? She would still flip, but the wording is different.

The Operative

The Heroes cannot win the game.
When The Operative is reduced to 0 or fewer HP, flip The Operative's Character card.
Whenever a Villain card is destroyed, The Operative deals the Hero with the highest HP (H) minus 2 Melee Damage.
At the end of the Villain turn, reveal cards from the top of the Villain deck until an Underboss card is revealed. Put it into play. Shuffle the rest of the revealed cards back into the Villain deck.

posts.name: Pydro
posts.cooked: Haka can only eat targets that are destroyed. If a target is destroyed, it will leave play and go to the trash. Many cards aren't destroyed but do something else instead. Operative, Ennead, and Heroes become incapped instead of being destroyed (they don't go to the trash), and Omnitron is removed from the game (and doesn't go to the trash). Therefore, cards like these aren't destroyed, and therefore can't be eaten by Haka.

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked:
Omnitron can go under Savage Mana, but then is immediately removed from the game. So the end result is the same. I believe in the 1.1 update we're simplifying that so it won't ask you.

The following is the result of our discussion with Christopher about this a little while back:

All the destroy triggers happen even if the card got put under another card (e.g. Savage Mana). So for Omnitron it would go under Savage Mana and then remove from the game. As another example, Pterodactyl Thief would go under Savage Mana and then cards would go to the owners hands.
